adjustment.analysis: Baseline median is 18.6. No events in target week. Price is up 6.2% (x1.062), which historically reduces demand. Past promotions show a median lift of x1.4, but the current price increase is not a promotion. The week after a promotion typically sees a 24% drop (x0.76), but no promotion occurred recently. Supplier delivery warning implies supply risk, which may reduce sales if stockouts occur. The noise-adjusted effect of price increases is not directly observed, but the price hike exceeds past promotions. The baseline trend is downward (-11.8% over 13 weeks). Evidence is limited but directional. Adjust down for price and supply risk.

brief:
PRODUCT: Cold & Flu Relief | category Health | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-22 (6 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 12.03 (+6.2% vs regular price 11.33)
  planner notes: Supplier warns of a short delivery

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 18.6 | 5%-95%: 2.9 - 39.3 | 10%-90%: 6.9 - 34.6

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-46% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
